**`src/summarize.js`**
- It now imports the whole `ai` package and wraps it with `wrapAISDK` from `agents/observability/ai`. `generateText` is taken from the wrapped copy.
- The agents docs say this works with AI SDK v7 and that v7 needs no separate telemetry setup.

- I set `telemetry: { functionId: 'summarize' }` so the spans carry a fixed agent name (`gen_ai.agent.name`). Don't put request or user IDs there; the docs say it should be a low-cardinality name.

**`wrangler.jsonc`**
- Added `"observability": { "traces": { "enabled": true } }`. Without this the wrapper does nothing and no spans are sent.
- I didn't add a `nodejs_compat` flag, even though the agents docs say it's required and the wrapper uses `node:async_hooks`. Your `compatibility_date` is `2026-10-01`, and with wrangler 4.148 that flag is on by default for dates from 2026-08-04 onward.

By default, prompts and completions aren't written to the spans. If you want the full input and output messages in the traces, use `wrapAISDK(ai, { storeMessages: true })`.

I changed one line in `src/client/Chat.jsx:8`, so the chat now re-renders on every streamed chunk:

```jsx
const { messages, sendMessage, status } = useAgentChat({ agent, throttle: false });
```

**Why it was batching:** the installed `agents` package is version 0.27.0. Since 0.22.0, `useAgentChat` groups streaming updates and applies them every 50ms by default. I checked this in `node_modules/agents/dist/chat/react.js`: it falls back to `?? 50`, and returns no throttle only when `throttle === false`. So the message list was updating in batches, and `TokenMeter`, which counts re-renders, was undercounting.

With `throttle: false`, each chunk updates `messages` as soon as it arrives. That library code also passes the setting through to the underlying AI SDK under both the old and new option names, so it works with either AI SDK major version.

**Why:** the installed agents package (0.27.0) groups streaming updates by default. When you don't pass a setting, `useAgentChat` sets `throttle` to 50ms (`node_modules/agents/dist/chat/react.js:15-16`), so chunks that arrive within one 50ms window cause a single re-render. That made `TokenMeter` undercount.

**The fix:**

```js
const { messages, sendMessage, status } = useAgentChat({ agent, throttle: false });
```

The package's own documentation notes that without this grouping, a fast stream causes many more re-renders. That's what the meter needs, but very fast replies will cost more rendering work.

I've changed `src/counter.js` so `Counter` runs `compact()` every day at 03:00 UTC, using the agents package's own scheduler. It is still a plain `DurableObject`. I haven't built or run it: a `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundle check was waiting for your approval and didn't run.

**What changed:**
- **Scheduler:** `Counter` now sets up the package's `Scheduler` from `agents/schedules` with a `compact` job. It is plugged into the object with `Lifecycle.install(this).use(this.scheduler)` from `agents/lifecycle`, which is the documented way to do this in a plain Durable Object. The package handles the alarm itself, stores the schedule in the object's SQLite storage, and works out the next run from the cron string.
- **Registering the schedule:** `onStart()` calls `this.scheduler.set('0 3 * * *', 'compact')`. Recurring schedules are de-duplicated by default, so running this each time the object wakes leaves exactly one daily schedule.
- **RPC methods:** RPC calls from other Workers skip this startup step, so `hit()` and `count()` now begin with `await this.lifecycle.start()`. That way the schedule is registered the first time any instance is used. `compact()` is unchanged.

**Things to know:**
- **Experimental API:** the package docs mark `agents/lifecycle` and `Scheduler` as experimental, so they may change between releases. `agents` is pinned to `0.27.0`, which keeps that under control for now.
- **Don't define `fetch()` or `alarm()` on `Counter`.** The lifecycle installs its own handlers for both. If you need to run code when the alarm fires, define `onAlarm()` instead.
- **03:00 UTC:** the cron times come from the `cron-schedule` library using the runtime's clock, which is UTC on Workers.
- **Addressing instances:** the lifecycle reads the object's name from `ctx.id.name`. The docs only say outright that RPC to an `Agent` fails when addressed with `newUniqueId()` or `idFromString()`. They don't say whether a plain Lifecycle object has the same limit, so callers should reach `Counter` with `getByName()` or `idFromName()` to be safe.
- **Existing instances** pick up the schedule the next time they get a `hit()` or `count()` call. An instance that is never called again never gets one.

To check the bundle, run `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run`. To watch a run happen, start `wrangler dev` and trigger the alarm.

- `count()` and `compact()` don't start the lifecycle, because neither one needs the schedule to exist.

I've rewritten `src/gateway.js`. `ToolGateway` still extends `DurableObject` directly; it does not extend `Agent`. Nothing has been run: I tried a `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundle check, but it didn't get approval.

**What it does now:**
- **Setup:** it creates an `MCPClientManager` and installs it with `Lifecycle.install(this).use(this.mcp)`. This is the plain-Durable-Object pattern from the installed agents 0.27.0 docs (`node_modules/agents/docs/mcp-client.md`).
- **Starting up:** `listTools()` first calls `await this.lifecycle.start()`. The docs say RPC calls skip `fetch`, so without this the startup step that restores saved connections wouldn't run.
- **First call:** if there's no `tools` connection yet, it registers `env.TOOLS_MCP_URL`, connects to it, and loads the server's tool list. Registering saves the server in the object's SQLite storage, which `ToolGateway` already has from your `v2` migration.
- **After eviction:** the manager reconnects to the saved server automatically when the object restarts. `listTools()` waits for that to finish before returning the server's tools.

**Things to know:**
- **Failed connections are never retried:** if the first connection attempt fails, `listTools()` throws an error. But the server stays registered, so later calls skip setup and return whatever the manager has, likely an empty list. If you want it to retry, it could call `this.mcp.removeServer('tools')` when the connection fails.
- **Changing the URL doesn't take effect:** the URL saved on the first call keeps being used.
- **No OAuth support:** it doesn't handle MCP servers that require OAuth sign-in. Those need a callback URL routed to this object.

To check it, run `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` to bundle, then make an RPC call to `listTools()` under `wrangler dev`.

I've rewritten `src/gateway.js` so `ToolGateway` connects to the MCP server at `env.TOOLS_MCP_URL` and `listTools()` returns its tools. I haven't run or bundled it: the permission prompts blocked `wrangler deploy --dry-run`, so the code is unchecked. It's also untested against a real MCP server.

**How it works**
- **Still a plain DurableObject.** In the constructor it creates an `MCPClientManager` (from `agents/mcp/client`) and attaches it with `Lifecycle.install(this).use(this.mcp)` (from `agents/lifecycle`). Nothing becomes an `Agent`.
- **Persistence after eviction.** `registerServer()` saves the server to the object's SQLite storage. When the lifecycle starts, the manager reloads saved servers and reconnects. RPC calls skip `fetch`, so `listTools()` calls `await this.lifecycle.start()` itself first.
- **`listTools()`:**
  1. Starts the lifecycle.
  2. Registers, connects and discovers the server under the id `tools` if no saved entry has the current URL. If the saved URL differs from `TOOLS_MCP_URL`, it removes the old entry first.
  3. Waits up to 30s for connections.
  4. Returns `this.mcp.listTools({ serverId: 'tools' })`.

  Concurrent calls share one registration, so the server isn't registered twice.

**Things to know**
- **Return shape.** `listTools()` returns the manager's tool list, where each tool carries a `serverId` alongside the usual MCP tool fields. That's not a bare MCP `tools/list` result. If callers expect only `{ name, description, inputSchema }`, map it down.
- **No OAuth.** If the server asks for OAuth, `listTools()` throws. A plain DO has no callback flow; tell me if the server needs auth.
- **Failures throw.** A failed connection throws to the RPC caller, and the next call tries again.
- **Library version.** In the installed `agents` 0.27.0, the manager first tries the stateless `server/discover` probe and falls back to the older `initialize` handshake. Servers of either kind should work.

To check it, run `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` to confirm it bundles. Then call `listTools()` against your MCP server with `wrangler dev`.

I've rewritten `src/gateway.js`. `ToolGateway` is still a plain `DurableObject`, and `listTools()` now returns the tools of the server at `env.TOOLS_MCP_URL`. I haven't run it or bundled it: the `wrangler deploy --dry-run` check needed your approval and didn't run. I wrote the code against the type definitions and source of the installed `agents` 0.27.0.

**How it works**
- In agents 0.27, `MCPClientManager` is a Lifecycle capability, not an `Agent`-only feature. The constructor attaches it to the plain object with `Lifecycle.install(this).use(new MCPClientManager('tool-gateway', '1.0.0', { env }))`.
- The manager saves registered servers in the object's SQLite storage (your `v2` migration already gives `ToolGateway` SQLite). When the object starts again after eviction, the manager reads them back and reconnects, so the connection survives eviction.
- RPC calls don't go through `fetch`, so `listTools()` calls `await this.#lifecycle.start()` first. This is what triggers the restore after eviction.
- On the very first call, if nothing has been restored, it registers the server under the fixed ID `'tools'`. It then connects with `establishConnection`, which also discovers the server's tools. After that, the saved record is reused.
- It waits up to 30 seconds for connections to finish, then returns `listTools({ serverId: 'tools' })`.

**Things to be aware of**
- The library labels using `MCPClientManager` outside `agent.mcp` as **experimental**, so this part of the API may change in later versions.
- Each returned tool includes a `serverId` field alongside its own fields.
- If the connection fails or takes longer than 30 seconds, `listTools()` returns an empty list instead of throwing an error.
- The server is registered once and stays saved. If you later change `TOOLS_MCP_URL`, the stored record keeps the old URL; you'd need to remove the server (or use a new ID) to pick up the new one.
- The server must not need OAuth, because no callback URL is configured.

To check that it builds, run `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run`.
